questions.q: What is the most common cause of a VLOOKUP silently returning a wrong answer instead of an error?
options: Omitting the 4th argument (range_lookup), which defaults to approximate match instead of exact match
Using too many rows of data
The lookup value being formatted in bold
VLOOKUP always throws an error when it's wrong, never a wrong answer
questions.explain: range_lookup defaults to TRUE (approximate match) if omitted — for exact-match lookups like IDs or SKUs, forgetting to pass FALSE is the classic silent-failure cause.

questions.q: Why does inserting a new column into a VLOOKUP's table_array silently break the formula?
options: col_index_num is a hardcoded position number, not a column name, so it now points at a different column
VLOOKUP automatically deletes itself when columns change
Excel disables VLOOKUP entirely after any column insertion
It doesn't break anything — VLOOKUP always adjusts automatically
questions.explain: col_index_num counts columns by position, not name — inserting a column shifts what's actually in that position without changing the number, so the formula quietly returns a different column's value.

questions.q: What can XLOOKUP do that VLOOKUP structurally cannot?
options: Look left — return a value from a column positioned to the left of the lookup column
Perform any kind of exact match at all
Reference more than one worksheet
Be used inside an IF function
questions.explain: VLOOKUP requires the lookup column to be the leftmost column of table_array. XLOOKUP's lookup_array and return_array are independent references, so it can look left just as easily as right.

questions.q: What does XLOOKUP's optional if_not_found argument do?
options: Returns a specified value directly when no match is found, instead of returning #N/A
Automatically fixes typos in the lookup value
Forces the lookup to always find a match, even a wrong one
Deletes the row if no match is found
questions.explain: if_not_found lets XLOOKUP return something like "Not found" directly on a missing match, which is a simpler alternative to wrapping the whole formula in IFERROR for that one case.

questions.q: Why hasn't XLOOKUP made VLOOKUP obsolete, according to this lesson?
options: XLOOKUP is only available in Excel 365/2021 and later — VLOOKUP still works in every older Excel version
XLOOKUP cannot perform exact matches
XLOOKUP is slower than VLOOKUP in every case
VLOOKUP is required by law in financial spreadsheets
questions.explain: If a workbook needs to open correctly in an older Excel install, XLOOKUP simply isn't available there yet — that compatibility gap is the real reason VLOOKUP is still relevant.
